rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-evidence/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.workflow`. The requirement says each skill MUST "open, before any other section, with its workflow as ordered steps".

**What conforms.** The file has a `## Workflow` section (`section[Habeas evidence]/section[Workflow]`). It is a numbered checklist, steps 1–8, so the steps are ordered.

**The gap.** The workflow does not come first. Under `# Habeas evidence`, two substantive paragraphs come before `## Workflow`:
- The first sets the testing and coverage artifact policy: use `habeas coverage`, run doctests separately, and never commit artifacts.
- The second is a separate procedure for post-suite `habeas coverage-check` failures. It says to tell measurement failures from coverage gaps, recollect, add tests or a `habeas:coverage` citation, and that `habeas:util` and `{fixme}` do not excuse coverage. It also says to use `habeas test` for full verification.

This is operational guidance, not a short orientation line. None of it is in the numbered steps. A reader gets a second set of instructions before the ordered workflow starts.

**Two readings.**
- Reading A: "section" means a heading-delimited section, and the unheaded preamble is not "another section". Under that reading the file conforms, because `## Workflow` is the first subsection.
- Reading B: the skill must open with the workflow, so substantive content before it breaks the obligation.

The wording supports both readings, and they lead to different verdicts. That ambiguity is itself a gap. Reading B is also the better fit for "open ... with its workflow", given how much procedure the preamble holds.

**Fix.** Move the preamble paragraphs after the workflow, for example into a section after `## Workflow`, or fold them into the workflow steps. Alternatively, tighten the requirement text to say what may precede the workflow. The other skills, such as `habeas-refactor`, put only a short explanatory intro before `## Workflow`.

No violation-query matches were listed for this site. No `{fixme}` acknowledges the gap.

**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed: the first determination was `true` with applies `true` and an independent second assessment's was `false` with applies `true`. A verifier checked the less favorable `false` with applies `true` determination and found an unacknowledged real gap, so `false` is recorded.

Verification:

**Applies.** `assets/skills/habeas-evidence/SKILL.md` has front matter (`name`, `description`) and sits under `assets/skills`. That makes it a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.workflow`.

**What conforms.** The file has `section[Habeas evidence]/section[Workflow]`. It is a numbered checklist of steps 1–8, so the steps are ordered. It is also the first headed section under the title. The same is true of every other bundled skill (`habeas`, `habeas-refactor`, `habeas-requirements`, `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`).

**Claimed gap: other procedure comes before the workflow.** The claim holds, in this form: the skill does not open with its workflow.
- Between `# Habeas evidence` and `## Workflow` sit two substantive paragraphs.
- The first sets the artifact policy: use `habeas coverage`, run doctests separately, never commit artifacts.
- The second is a separate procedure for `habeas coverage-check` failures. It covers recollecting measurement failures, adding tests or a `habeas:coverage` citation, `habeas:util` and `{fixme}` not excusing coverage, and using `habeas test`.
- None of this is in the numbered steps. A reader gets a second set of instructions before the ordered workflow.
- The requirement says each skill MUST "open, before any other section, with its workflow as ordered steps". Opening with the workflow means it comes first, ahead of other content. These paragraphs are not a short orientation line, and they displace it.

**Ambiguity.** There is a narrower reading. Under it "section" means only a headed section, and an unheaded preamble is not "another section", so the file conforms. The wording "open … with its workflow" supports the other reading at least as well: the first thing in the skill is the workflow. The two readings give different verdicts, so the ambiguity is itself a gap, and the text should say what may precede the workflow. On the better reading the file also breaks the requirement outright.

**Violation queries.** None were listed for this site.

**Acknowledgment.** I found no `{fixme}` reference for this gap, so it is not acknowledged.

**Fix.** Move the two paragraphs after `## Workflow`, for example into a section or into the workflow steps. Otherwise tighten the requirement to state what may precede the workflow.
